evals.name: implicit-decision-during-change
evals.prompt: Our jobs get lost every time the jobs-service restarts because the queue in src/jobs/queue.ts is just an in-memory array. Make the queue durable so jobs survive restarts. Keep it simple, it's one instance on a small VM. Don't implement it yet, I want to agree on the approach first, but put whatever we need in the repo so we remember why we chose it.
evals.expected_output: An ADR added as docs/adr/0003-*.md following the existing Nygard-style ADRs, comparing real options (e.g. a Postgres-backed queue using the existing database vs. Redis/BullMQ vs. a hosted queue), choosing one with reasons tied to the single-instance/small-VM/Postgres-already-present context, stating costs, with status proposed. No queue implementation yet.

assertions.text: Exactly one new ADR is added as docs/adr/0003-<kebab-title>.md
The ADR lists at least two options and at least one negative consequence

assertions: The ADR's status is proposed (or equivalent), not accepted, because the user has not agreed yet
The decision rationale refers to the project's actual context: a single instance, a small VM, and PostgreSQL already in use

evals.name: supersede-existing-decision
evals.prompt: we're moving notify-app off polling, the 5s lag annoys people and we now have ~2k users. going with server-sent events from a small node service next to the next.js app. can you write the decision up properly? docs/decisions is where these live
evals.expected_output: A new docs/decisions/0002-*.md recording the move to SSE with context (user growth, latency), options (keep polling, SSE, WebSockets, hosted push), consequences including operational costs of long-lived connections; 0001 marked superseded by 0002 with its original decision text intact; index README updated.

assertions.text: 0001 is marked superseded with its decision text intact, 0002 is added, links back, and the index is updated
The new ADR lists at least two options and at least one negative consequence

assertions: The new ADR's status is accepted, because the user has already decided
The consequences mention an operational cost of long-lived connections (hosting limits, connection counts, or reconnect handling)
The new ADR follows the field style of 0001 (bullet Status/Date fields, same heading names) rather than a different template

evals.name: trivial-change-no-adr
evals.prompt: add a --delimiter option to csv-tool so I can read semicolon separated files, default stays comma
evals.expected_output: The --delimiter flag implemented in csvtool/__main__.py with comma default. No ADR or decision document created, since this is a small, easily reversible change.

assertions.text: python -m csvtool --delimiter ';' reads a semicolon file correctly
No ADR or decision record was created

evals.name: implicit-adr-session-store
evals.prompt: users keep getting logged out randomly — I think it's because we run 2 instances and sessions live in memory. move sessions somewhere shared. we already have postgres
evals.expected_output: express-session configured with a shared store (e.g. connect-pg-simple on the existing Postgres, with the session table created), and, without being asked, docs/adr/0002-*.md in the 0001 style recording the decision: context (two instances, in-memory sessions, random logouts), options (Postgres store, Redis, sticky sessions, stateless tokens), the choice and why, and costs (extra DB writes per request, session table cleanup).

assertions.text: A shared session store is configured and a new ADR 0002 records the decision with options and a cost

assertions: The ADR follows 0001's structure (bullet Status/Date fields and the same three headings)
The response tells the user that an ADR was added and why
